Part 1 · NM-FW01 — the WireGuard tunnel on pfSense (OPNsense on the last frame)

≈ 20 min
  1. System > Package Manager > Available Packages → install WireGuard (OPNsense: already in the core).
  2. VPN > WireGuard > Tunnels > Add Tunnel: Enable · Listen Port 51820 · Generate keys (copy the public key) · Interface Addresses 10.66.0.1/24 · Save.
  3. VPN > WireGuard > Peers > Add Peer: Enable · the client public key · Allowed IPs 10.66.0.2/32 · Dynamic Endpoint · Save.
  4. Firewall > Rules > WAN > Add: Pass · UDP · destination WAN address · port 51820 · Save · Apply Changes.
  5. Firewall > Rules > WireGuard: Pass ICMP 10.66.0.0/24 → 192.168.20.0/24; Pass TCP 10.66.0.0/24 → 192.168.20.10 ports 443, 445; the rest is denied by default.
  6. VPN > WireGuard > Settings: Enable WireGuard → Save. Snapshot NM-FW01.
  7. OPNsense 26.7: VPN > WireGuard > Instances / Peers / General, then the same two rules.
Version note (September–October 2026):
  • pfSense CE 2.9.0 (verified September 2026): WireGuard is an add-on package; its tabs are Tunnels, Peers, Settings and Status. Older screenshots found online (2.5/2.6) show the same fields in a slightly different layout.
  • OPNsense: WireGuard has been part of the core since 24.1. Older how-tos tell you to install the os-wireguard plugin — on 26.7 that step no longer exists.

Part 1 · NM-RW01 — the remote worker client

≈ 15 min
  1. sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y wireguard
  2. umask 077; wg genkey | sudo tee /etc/wireguard/rw01.key | wg pubkey | sudo tee /etc/wireguard/rw01.pub → paste the PUBLIC key in the pfSense peer.
  3. Write /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf: [Interface] PrivateKey, Address 10.66.0.2/32 · [Peer] the firewall public key, Endpoint 198.51.100.10:51820, AllowedIPs 10.66.0.0/24, 192.168.20.0/24, PersistentKeepalive 25.
  4. sudo wg-quick up wg0
  5. sudo wg show → "latest handshake: … seconds ago" is the proof that both key pairs match.
  6. ping -c 3 10.66.0.1 and ping -c 3 192.168.20.10 — both answer because of the WireGuard-tab rules.
Version note (September–October 2026):
  • Ubuntu Server 26.04.1 LTS: the package is simply "wireguard"; the kernel support is built in. A newer Ubuntu LTS uses the same commands.
  • Windows remote worker instead: install the official WireGuard client from wireguard.com, "Add empty tunnel", paste the same [Interface]/[Peer] text, Activate — the GUI shows the same handshake and transfer counters.

Part 2A · The encrypted ClientRecords container — VeraCrypt 1.26.29

≈ 25 min
  1. Volumes > Create New Volume → "Create an encrypted file container" → Next.
  2. Standard VeraCrypt volume → Select File… → ClientRecords.hc (beside the folder, never inside it).
  3. Encryption Algorithm AES · Hash Algorithm SHA-512 (default; Argon2id accepted).
  4. Volume Size 200 MB · a laboratory passphrase of 20+ characters (write "lab passphrase" in the chapter).
  5. Move the mouse until the bar fills → Format.
  6. Mount ClientRecords.hc as V: → copy the ClientRecords folder in → Dismount. Delete the plaintext copy only after it opens from V:.
  7. Tools > Backup Volume Header to a file kept APART from the container (your recovery plan); test a WRONG passphrase → refused (screenshot).
Version note (September–October 2026):
  • VeraCrypt 1.26.29 (June 9, 2026, veracrypt.io — veracrypt.fr redirects there) added Argon2id as an alternative key derivation for non-system volumes; older 1.26.x builds list only the PBKDF2 hashes. The wizard pages are otherwise identical.
  • BitLocker alternative on Windows Server 2025: the feature is not installed by default — Install-WindowsFeature BitLocker … -Restart first, then Enable-BitLocker on a DATA volume (E:) with -RecoveryPasswordProtector.

Part 2B · HTTPS on the intranet with a self-signed certificate (IIS path, nginx path, trust on NM-WS01)

≈ 25 min
  1. NM-FS01: Install-WindowsFeature Web-Server; New-SelfSignedCertificate with the SAN (DNS name + IP address), EKU serverAuth, ECDSA P-256, 200 days.
  2. New-WebBinding https 443 + AddSslCertificate(thumbprint); Remove-WebBinding http 80 → HTTPS only.
  3. Export-Certificate → intranet.cer (public only); certutil -hashfile intranet.cer SHA256 = the fingerprint.
  4. Linux path on NM-LX01: set SVC_IP, then sudo bash nm_https_enable.sh (key + certificate, HTTPS-only nginx, 5 tests, registry line).
  5. NM-WS01: compare the SHA-256 on both machines → Import-Certificate into Cert:\LocalMachine\Root.
  6. Edge: https:// padlock, no warning; http:// refused (IIS) or 301 (nginx). Never click past a warning.
  7. Register the certificate: expiry, renewal = expiry − 30 days, fingerprint, key location (Chapter 5 registry).
Version note (September–October 2026):
  • Windows Server 2025 and Windows 11 25H2 (verified September 2026): the PKI and WebAdministration cmdlets are unchanged since Server 2022; IIS Manager looks the same. A newer Edge build may word the certificate warning differently — the fix is always the import, never the "proceed" link.
  • OpenSSL on the Ubuntu 26.04 VM: run "openssl version" — the script works on every supported line (3.5 LTS, 3.6, 4.0); only the version string in your screenshots will differ from the kit.

Part 3 · Proving it — two captures, the canary, HTTPS-only, the locked container, the evidence table

≈ 30 min
  1. NM-FW01: Diagnostics > Packet Capture — Interface WAN, UDP, port 51820, Count 200 → Start.
  2. NM-RW01: curl http://intranet.northmaple.internal/NM-CANARY-1710 and one https:// request → Stop → Download → wan_capture.pcap; repeat on tun_wg0 → tunnel_wg0.pcap.
  3. Wireshark, wan_capture.pcap: udp.port == 51820 shows only "WireGuard"; Find Packet "NM-CANARY" → not found.
  4. Wireshark, tunnel_wg0.pcap: the canary IS readable in the HTTP request (positive control). Diagnostics > Command Prompt: wg show → wg_show_fw01.txt.
  5. curl http:// → 301 or refused, never 200; openssl s_client … -CAfile intranet.crt -brief → TLSv1.3, Verification: OK.
  6. Container dismounted: findstr / grep for the marker → nothing in ClientRecords.hc, found in a plaintext file (control); wrong passphrase refused.
  7. python3 nm_validate_encryption.py with all files in one folder → 14 PASS, 1 MANUAL → paste C17_validation_evidence.md into 6.4.
Version note (September–October 2026):
  • Wireshark 4.6.x (current September 2026) labels the protocol "WireGuard"; 4.4 and 3.6 show it the same way. If you see only "UDP", update Wireshark.
  • pfSense 2.9.0 Packet Capture page: the Download button appears after Stop; OPNsense 26.7 exposes captures as downloadable jobs under Interfaces > Diagnostics > Packet capture.

What a real pair of captures looks like

This is not a mock-up: it was built from the two actual capture files of the Class 17 recorded run. Each tunnel packet is shown twice — on the firewall's WAN interface (an unreadable WireGuard transport message) and on wg0 after decryption (the canary and the service name readable). Your own captures in Part 3 will look like this, with your own addresses and counters.

Recorded October 10, 2026 · Ubuntu 24.04 · wireguard-go · nginx 1.24 · tcpdump 4.99 — the on-wire format is identical with the pfSense or OPNsense WireGuard of your lab.
